Following the release of the seventh developer betas for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and Apple's other upcoming software updates, Apple is now rolling out the corresponding public beta versions to its public beta channel. Here are the details.

Apple Releases New Public Beta Versions

Apple earlier today released the following builds:

  • iOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate Developer Beta 7 (Build 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build 24R5358a)

Apple is now pushing the corresponding builds out to the public beta channel, marking the fifth public beta release for this cycle. So far, Apple has released new public betas for iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's release doesn't include any particularly notable changes, as Apple is now primarily focused on bug fixes and stability improvements in the final weeks leading up to the official launch.

Additionally, Apple today also released the second release candidate (RC) of macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20), having previously pushed the corresponding developer RC build earlier today. The second RC of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is also expected to arrive shortly, and became available at 7:42 PM Eastern Time.

Across all of today's releases, the public beta builds share the same version numbers as their corresponding developer counterparts.

Enroll in the Apple Beta Program

To enroll your device in the public beta program, visit https://beta.apple.com and follow the instructions to register each of your devices. Here's how to install the public beta on your iPhone:

  • Go to the Apple Beta Software Program website and select "Sign Up" or "Sign In".
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone, then accept the program terms and enroll your account.
  • Open Settings on your iPhone.
  • Go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates.
  • Select "iOS 27 Public Beta".
  • Return to the Software Update page, and once the public beta appears, tap "Update Now".

Apple recommends installing beta software on a non-primary device. If you install it on your main iPhone, make sure you have a recent backup beforehand.

Have you spotted any changes in today's public beta? Let us know in the comments.
